properties.name: Escalation from drift is computed — but probably NOT from a single scalar
properties.statement:
REASSESSED 2026-07-28, same day, on Anthony's instruction not to treat reflow's workflows as canon. This requirement was first written as "drift rolls up to one number, and how far the work retreats is computed from it", arguing from reflow's scalar drift_score. That argument was too credulous and the name has been changed with it. What follows keeps the real question and demotes reflow's answer to one option among several.

THE REAL QUESTION, which stands on its own: when the design and the build have diverged, nothing in reflow2 says HOW FAR BACK the work should go. Per-event dispositions answer "what do we do about this divergence"; nothing answers "is the accumulated divergence bad enough that we should stop adding to it and revisit the allocation, or the intent?" That question is real and unanswered.

WHY THE SCALAR IS THE WEAK PART. Collapsing heterogeneous drift into one 0.0-1.0 number destroys precisely the information that decides what to do: a missing artifact, a spec mismatch and an undocumented addition are different problems with different responses, and their average is not a thing. reflow's thresholds (below 0.3 keep building, 0.3 to 0.5 revise allocation, at or above 0.5 revise intent) are invented numbers with no derivation given, and its retreat targets are phase-shaped because reflow had phases. Adopting the scalar would also collide with dec:certainty-derived: a confident aggregate computed from a base the code already disagrees with is an assertion dressed as a measurement.

reflow2 IS ALREADY AHEAD HERE AND SHOULD NOT REGRESS. Drift is disposed of PER EVENT — design_holds or design_updated — so a session can hold the design on one divergence and update it on another, which reflow's single global mode could not do. And confirm.rs audits whether the dispositions are honest: "five design_holds claims with zero design edits is a very different confirmation history from one design_updated". That history is a better signal than any scalar, because it is evidence rather than an estimate. If escalation is built, it should read the disposition history, not an average.

THE PRECONDITION STILL HOLDS whatever shape is chosen: DriftEvent.severity is one of the WRITTEN-and-never-consulted properties the 2026-07-28 sweep found — written from kind.severity() at three call sites while ranking re-derives it via severity_rank(kind) — so any computation over stored severity reads a value the code already contradicts. Settle the single-source question first.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WANTED, stated without borrowing reflow's mechanism: a computed, evidence-backed answer to "should we keep building or go back, and back to WHAT" — where the destinations are layers of the golden thread (realization, allocation, intent) rather than phases, and the trigger is drawn from what the graph can already prove (unresolved DriftEvents by kind, the design_holds/design_updated history, coverage moving the wrong way) rather than from a number nobody can derive. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows; reassessed the same day.
